_about: Machine-readable form of hardware/br8d-catalogue.md. Each module lists its folder, size, occupied pairs and files. Fields with null or empty values are for the design and sourcing workflow to fill in.
title: br8d adapter module catalogue
notes: Find your connector: container (heading 1), application (heading 2), family (heading 3), then the module (heading 4). Module names link to their proposed folders. The maps are proposals; nothing here is built yet. The size token (`1u` or `2u`) gives the board width in 1U units.

families.name: br8d-i-aux
notes: Maps: TS: A: tip / sleeve. TRS stereo: A: tip (left) / sleeve; B: ring (right) / sleeve. TRS balanced: A: tip / ring; sleeve to a separate shield. TRRS (provisional): A: tip / ring 1; V: ring 2 / sleeve.
Use 3.5 mm sockets for these; a 2.5 mm socket needs its own name and footprint.

TRRS needs a `br8d-o-patch` lead. The sleeve makes contact first, and the contacts can short during insertion. A three-pole plug shorts V and is not a valid power signature. CTIA and OMTP headsets swap ring 2 and sleeve, so a headset is not a br8d lead.
One TS socket on A.
One TS socket on B.
Two TS sockets, one per pair.
Four TS sockets, one per pair. V signal use is open.
Shared AUX/CV I/O with level 1 protection. Circuit and power are undecided.
One stereo TRS socket: left on A, right on B.
First stereo socket on A/B, second on C/V. Tip is the first pair's +, ring the second pair's +, and the sleeve joins both returns. V signal use is open.
One balanced TRS socket on A.
Four balanced TRS sockets, one per pair. Sleeves go to a separate shield.
One TRRS socket, provisional map as above.

families.name: br8d-i-cv
notes: Connector: 3.5 mm TS for modular CV, gate and clock.
The single-socket CV boards are the AUX TS boards in a CV-labelled box, so they share a design (see [Design inheritance](#design-inheritance)).
The TRS and TRRS CV layouts are new, not the AUX map. The four-TRS shield needs its own path, and tying the two-TRRS sleeves together would join B- and V-.
One socket on A. Same board as `br8d-i-aux-1ts-br0-1u-A`.
One socket on B. Same board as `br8d-i-aux-1ts-br0-1u-B`.
Two sockets, one per pair.
Four sockets, one per pair. V use is open.
Four TRS sockets, tip / ring to + / -, sleeves to a separate shield. Same map as the balanced AUX board.

Two TRRS sockets: A on tip / ring 1 with B on ring 2 / sleeve; C on tip / ring 1 with V on ring 2 / sleeve (proposed). Whether the sleeves also go to shield is undecided. Not the AUX TRRS profile, so it needs its own parent.
Active CV I/O with level 1 protection. Circuit, power source and direction are not designed yet.

families.name: br8d-i-jack
notes: Maps: TS: A: tip / sleeve. TRS stereo: A: tip (left) / sleeve; B: ring (right) / sleeve. TRS balanced: A: tip / ring; sleeve to a separate shield.
Insert jacks often use tip and ring for send and return. Those need their own profile.
One TS socket on A.
One TS socket on B.
One stereo TRS socket: left on A, right on B.
Two stereo sockets: first on A/B, second on C/V. Sleeves join their returns. V use is open.
One balanced TRS socket on A.
One balanced TRS socket on B.

families.name: br8d-i-rca
notes: Map: each socket is tip to + and sleeve to -. Left is usually white (sometimes black), right red, video yellow.
The 2- and 4-socket boards serve as mono or stereo; the pairs decide which.
A composite board combines more than one connector. Count independent pairs, not sockets. A shared pair ties its contacts together, so it is not another channel. One 2x4 header has only four pairs.

Three RCA sockets (left, right, video) use A, B and C. An independent stereo TRS socket needs two more pairs, five in total. Alternatives: mirror repeats RCA stereo on TRS, so don't connect independent outputs to both; mono keeps the three RCA signals but gives up TRS stereo and the power pair; dropping video frees C for a stereo TRS pair on C/V; two br8d headers give five pairs but need a multi-header naming and pin convention, because the `-ABCV` suffix can't say which header owns a pair.
One RCA socket on A.
Two RCA sockets, one per pair. Stereo is left on A, right on B.
Four RCA sockets, one per pair. V use is open.
Composite video trio: left on A, right on B, video on C (proposed). Mixed RCA and TRS layouts are the 3rcaAV1trs modules below.
Left on A, right on B, video on C. TRS tip to A+, ring to B+, sleeve to A- and B-. The TRS repeats the RCA stereo pair; it does not add channels.
Left on A, right on B, video on C. TRS tip / sleeve on V+ / V-, ring unused. This keeps all three RCA signals but gives up the power pair.
`mirror` and `mono` distinguish layouts that the pair suffix alone can't describe.

families.name: br8d-i-phono
notes: Map: left on A, right on B, each tip / sleeve. Earth lug goes to a separate shield contact (proposed).
A moving-magnet cartridge is sensitive to load. Pick the gain and loading stage in the endpoint, not on the breakout.
Two RCA sockets with a separate earth-lug connection.

families.name: br8d-i-xlr
notes: Map: pin 2 (hot) on + and pin 3 (cold) on -; pin 1 is shield.
Audio XLR and DMX XLR swap pins 2 and 3 on A, so their boards are not interchangeable. Check the device before plugging in.
Phantom power puts +48 V on both signal pins relative to pin 1. Ribbon mics and some older line gear don't like it, so switch phantom off unless the mic needs it.
Female XLR-3 on A.
Female XLR-3 on B.
Male XLR-3 on A.
Male XLR-3 on B.

containers.name: Speakers
notes: Speaker outputs can carry tens of volts and enough current to damage a small endpoint. Treat them as level 4-5 work and check the amplifier's output before connecting anything.

families.name: br8d-i-speaker-pas
notes: Map (NL8): A: pin 1+ / 1- (sub); B: pin 2+ / 2- (low); C: pin 3+ / 3- (mid); V: pin 4+ / 4- (high).
V carries a speaker signal, not power. The V power rules do not fit this case and need an exemption.
The NL4, NL2, banana and binding-post boards below are proposals. Each connector's pair allocation for two-way and one-way speakers is still open.
NL4 is likely too wide for 1U; check the datasheet. NL2 is proposed on 1U.

connector.description: Speakon NL8/NL4/NL2, banana or binding post (per module)

notes: Speakon NL8, four pairs.
Speakon NL4 (proposed): 1+ / 1- on A, 2+ / 2- on B.
Speakon NL2 (proposed): 1+ / 1- on A.
One pair of 4 mm banana sockets: + on A+, - on A-.
Two banana pairs, one per speaker: left on A, right on B.
One pair of binding posts: red on A+, black on A-.
Two binding-post pairs, one per speaker.

families.name: br8d-i-speaker-pow
notes: Signal profile, not a connector map: A: left+ / left-; B: right+ / right-; C: sub+ / sub-; V: power+ / power-.
No connector is chosen yet, so no variant is proposed. Pick a four-pair connector, then define levels, power and the endpoint before drawing a board.

applications.name: MIDI
notes: MIDI is a 5 mA current loop, one direction per cable. Type A and Type B TRS swap tip and ring, so check which one a lead is before connecting it. The shield is conventionally bonded at the OUT end, so a MIDI IN socket does not connect DIN pin 2. A legacy MIDI OUT is a foreign source, not a br8d peer.

families.name: br8d-i-midi
notes: DIN-5 (180 degrees): A: pin 4 (source) / pin 5 (sink); shield: pin 2.
TRS Type A: A: ring (source) / tip (sink); shield: sleeve.
TRS Type B: A: tip (source) / ring (sink); shield: sleeve.
Each socket is one direction; the endpoint decides which role it plays.
One female DIN-5 on A.
One female DIN-5 on B; pin 2 to a separate shield.
Two female DIN-5 sockets, one per pair.
One 3.5 mm TRS Type A socket on A.
Two TRS Type A sockets, one per pair.
One 3.5 mm TRS Type B socket on A.
Two TRS Type B sockets, one per pair.

applications.name: S/PDIF, AES3 and word clock
notes: Coax and balanced digital audio. Use 75 ohm BNC or the correct XLR for the rate in use.

families.name: br8d-i-spdif
notes: RCA (usually orange) or 3.5 mm TS: A: tip / sleeve.
BNC, 75 ohm: A: centre / shell.

connector.description: RCA, 3.5 mm TS or BNC (per module)

notes: One RCA socket on A.
Two RCA sockets, one per pair.
One 3.5 mm TS socket on A.
Two 3.5 mm TS sockets, one per pair.
One BNC socket on A.
One BNC socket on B.

families.name: br8d-i-aes
notes: AES3 balanced, 110 ohm XLR-3: A: pin 2 (+) / pin 3 (-); shield: pin 1.
AES3id, 75 ohm BNC: A: centre / shell.
Female XLR-3 on A.
Female XLR-3 on B.
Male XLR-3 on A.
Male XLR-3 on B.
One BNC socket on A.
One BNC socket on B.

families.name: br8d-i-wclk
notes: Word clock, 75 ohm BNC: A: centre / shell.
One BNC socket on A.
One BNC socket on B.

applications.name: Optical: TOSLINK and ADAT
notes: Light, not wire, so the board maps the transceiver's electrical side, not the optical port. ADAT (eight channels at 48 kHz) uses the same TOSLINK transceiver.

families.name: br8d-i-toslink
notes: Transceiver electrical side: A: TX data / GND; B: RX data / GND; V: VCC / GND.
Check the module's logic and supply voltage (commonly 3.3 V or 5 V) before wiring to a node.
One TOSLINK transceiver module on the header.

families.name: br8d-i-dmx
notes: XLR-5: A: pin 3 (Data 1+) / pin 2 (Data 1-); B: pin 5 (Data 2+) / pin 4 (Data 2-); shield: pin 1.
XLR-3 fixtures: A: pin 3 (Data+) / pin 2 (Data-); shield: pin 1.
DMX swaps pins 2 and 3 on A relative to audio XLR. See [XLR](#balanced-xlr).
Female XLR-5, both data pairs.
Male XLR-5, both data pairs.
Female XLR-3 on A.
Male XLR-3 on A.
Male XLR-3 on B.

families.name: br8d-i-led
notes: Connector: addressable LEDs, JST-SM or similar. Check the strip's pinout first.
Map: A: data / clock; V: 5 V / GND. WS2812 uses data only, so A- is left open. APA102 and SK9822 use data and clock.
Long strips need a power injector. The 500 mA V supply target is provisional.
Three contacts: data and power.
Four contacts: data, clock and power.
Two four-contact sockets on A and B share V power. Current is shared; neither output is isolated.

families.name: br8d-o-usb
notes: A br8d port is only USB if the endpoint speaks USB. Real hosts and chargers are foreign sources.
Profile names from the connection guide map to these boards: `br8d-o-A` / `-A-3`, `-B` / `-B-3`, `-B-mini`, `-B-micro`, `-C` / `-C-4`.
USB 2.0 A and B: A: pin 3 D+ / pin 2 D-; V: pin 1 VBUS / pin 4 GND; shield: shell.
USB-C: A: A6/B6 D+ / A7/B7 D-; V: A4, A9, B4, B9 VBUS / A1, A12, B1, B12 GND; shield: shell.
Mini/micro ID and USB 3.x pin 7 GND_DRAIN are not mapped.

connector.description: USB-A, B, B mini/micro or C (per module)

notes: USB-A 2.0 receptacle.
USB-A 3.x receptacle. B: pin 9 SSTX+ / pin 8 SSTX-; C: pin 6 SSRX+ / pin 5 SSRX-.
USB-B 2.0 receptacle, square.
USB-B 3.x receptacle. B: pin 9 SSRX+ / pin 8 SSRX-; C: pin 6 SSTX+ / pin 5 SSTX-. B is host-to-device and C device-to-host.
Mini-B receptacle. V: pin 1 VBUS / pin 5 GND.
Micro-B receptacle. V: pin 1 VBUS / pin 5 GND.
USB-C receptacle, USB 2.0 cable, two-pair profile. Do not drive VBUS before the endpoint has identified itself; leave CC unconnected for now.
USB-C receptacle, full-featured cable, four-pair profile. B: A2 TX1+ / A3 TX1-; C: B11 RX1+ / B10 RX1-.
Open: the B/C SuperSpeed lanes swap when the plug is flipped. SBU is unmapped.

applications.name: Thunderbolt
notes: Thunderbolt 3 and 4 use the USB-C connector. The power and USB 2.0 contacts follow the [USB-C](#usb-ports) boards above. The high-speed lanes need a dedicated design, so no header-based Thunderbolt board is proposed.

families.name: br8d-cat-rj45
notes: Profiles: `br8d-o-cat` connector, `br8d-i-lan` interface.
Map: A: pin 1 / pin 2; B: pin 3 / pin 6; C: pin 4 / pin 5; V: pin 7 / pin 8. Shield: socket shell, if present.
Straight-through cable in T568B at both ends. A crossover swaps A and B.
Passive PoE mode B uses C and V as joined power rails, so they are not four independent pairs.
One RJ45 socket.

families.name: br8d-i-lan
notes: M12 D-coded, four-pin industrial Ethernet. Map: A: pin 1 / pin 3; B: pin 2 / pin 4; shield: housing.
One M12 D-coded four-pin connector. Choose contact gender and mounting for the panel.

families.name: br8d-i-rj11
notes: Map (6P contacts numbered 1-6 left to right, clip down): line 1 on pins 3 (tip) and 4 (ring). Pins 2 and 5 are unused on RJ11. RJ14 adds line 2 on pins 2 and 5; RJ12 uses the outer pins for key-system control, not a second line.
Use: handset cords, phone-to-phone test leads, or your own line interface.
Do not connect a board to a live telephone line. Lines can carry about 48 V DC, and ringing reaches about 90 V RMS. Telephone network connections are regulated in most countries.
One RJ11 socket; line 1 on A.
One RJ12 socket; line 1 on A. RJ12 is a single line, so there is no second pair to map.

families.name: br8d-i-com
notes: FTDI TTL-232R six-pin, host side: A: pin 4 TXD / pin 5 RXD; B: pin 6 RTS# / pin 2 CTS#; V: pin 3 VCC / pin 1 GND.
DE-9 RS-232, DTE (PC) side: A: pin 3 TXD / pin 2 RXD; B: pin 7 RTS / pin 8 CTS; C: pin 4 DTR / pin 6 DSR; V: - / pin 5 GND; shield: shell.
VCC is 3.3 V or 5 V, depending on the device. RS-232 swings about +/-5 to +/-15 V; a TTL or FTDI-level port will not work with it.

connector.description: FTDI 6-pin header or DE-9 male (per module)

notes: One six-pin FTDI TTL-232R header, host side.
One male DE-9, DTE-style pins. DTE and DCE swap TXD and RXD. DCD and RI are unmapped.

families.name: br8d-i-can
notes: DE-9 CAN, CiA 303-1: A: pin 7 CAN_H / pin 2 CAN_L; V: pin 9 CAN_V+ (optional) / pin 3 CAN_GND; shield: pin 5 CAN_SHLD.
CAN_V+ is nominally 7-13 V when supplied.
One male DE-9. Specify the optional V+ connection when designing.

families.name: br8d-i-485
notes: RS-485 terminal block: A: D+ / D- (vendor labels vary, and TIA calls D+ "B"); V: - / GND (common); shield: shield terminal.
V- is a common reference for the bus, not a power supply.
Four terminals: D+, D-, common and shield. Four 5.08 mm terminals are about 20 mm wide, so 2U leaves room for the enclosure clearance.
Two terminal blocks on the same bus and shield. Termination and topology are external.

families.name: br8d-i-qwic
notes: Qwiic / STEMMA QT, four-pin JST-SH. Map (provisional): A: pin 3 SDA / pin 4 SCL; V: pin 2 3.3 V / pin 1 GND.
Qwiic is **3.3 V only**. Plugging a 5 V device into it can damage the sensor, so use a 3.3 V port or a level-shifting bridge.
One four-pin JST-SH socket.
Two sockets on the same SDA, SCL, 3.3 V and GND lines. Check combined current and pull-ups.

families.name: br8d-i-grove
notes: Grove four-pin: A: pin 2 / pin 1; V: pin 3 VCC / pin 4 GND. Check the device for 3.3 V or 5 V.
One four-pin Grove socket.
Two sockets sharing all four lines. Check voltage, current and pull-ups.

applications.name: Display sideband
notes: Video itself runs on high-speed differential pairs that a 2x4 header can't carry. These boards map the low-speed sideband: EDID, hot-plug and power.

families.name: br8d-i-hdmi
notes: HDMI 19-pin sideband: A: pin 16 DDC SDA / pin 15 DDC SCL; B: pin 19 HPD / pin 13 CEC; V: pin 18 +5 V / pin 17 GND.
Sources supply about 50 mA on +5 V.
One HDMI 19-pin socket, sideband only.

families.name: br8d-i-dp
notes: DisplayPort 20-pin sideband: A: pin 15 AUX+ / pin 17 AUX- (differential, not single-ended); B: pin 18 HPD / pin 13 CONFIG1; V: pin 20 DP_PWR (3.3 V) / pin 19 GND.
One DisplayPort 20-pin socket, sideband only.

families.name: br8d-o-flat
notes: 2x4 keyed, shrouded IDC, 2.54 mm ribbon. Map: A: pin 1 / pin 2; B: pin 3 / pin 4; C: pin 5 / pin 6; V: pin 7 / pin 8. The red stripe marks pin 1.
`br8d-o-flat-8` in this catalogue is this profile. A board here is a header-to-header breakout or pass-through. Rotation maps pin n to pin 9-n.
2x4 header-to-header pass-through.
Two parallel headers. All conductors are shared, not isolated.
2x5 to 2x4 pass-through. Pins 9 and 10 are proposed for shield, and the shield path is still open.

families.name: br8d-i-eurorack
notes: Eurorack 10-pin IDC (Doepfer style): pin 1 -12 V (red stripe), pin 2 GND, pin 9 GND, pin 10 +12 V. The 16-pin variant with +5 V is not mapped.
Map: A: -12 V / GND; V: +12 V / GND. The two GND returns join at the board.
The ribbon can be fitted backwards on a loose header. Check the stripe before you power up, because a reversed rail can damage modules.
One 10-pin IDC for the Eurorack bus, two pairs on the header.

families.name: br8d-i-pwr
notes: 5.5 x 2.1 mm DC barrel, power only. Map: V: centre / sleeve.
Centre-positive is common, but centre-negative exists. Check the supply's polarity and voltage.
One 5.5 x 2.1 mm barrel jack.

applications.name: Mains and IEC
notes: Mains never goes on a br8d header. Use a ready-made IEC inlet with a certified power module, and keep low-voltage DC on the [DC power](#dc-power) board.

applications.name: Combo XLR/TRS sockets
notes: A combo socket's contacts depend on which plug is inserted, so there is no single map. Use the XLR-3 board for balanced XLR or the TRS board for jack.

applications.name: Cable forms
notes: Twin flex (`br8d-o-flex`), shielded multicore (`br8d-o-shield`), unshielded loom (`br8d-o-loom`), M12 (`br8d-o-m12`) and community connectors (`br8d-o-x`) are cable or connector families, not defined maps. Twin flex carries one pair: A for a signal, or V for power.

applications.name: Reading the maps
notes: Each module name is a proposed folder, relative to this file. Unless noted, the board connects a keyed, shrouded 2x4 2.54 mm header to the named connector. Folders sit under their family folder, with the name after the family prefix.

Header pin:  1   2   3   4   5   6   7   8
Conductor:  A+  A-  B+  B-  C+  C-  V+  V-

`A: X / Y` means A+ connects to X and A- to Y; B, C and V follow the same pattern. `-` means no external contact. Pin numbers are the connector's own contacts. Check the footprint and cable with a continuity test before use.

A repeated contact joins its header conductors, so stereo sleeves share a return. A **shield** listed in an entry is a separate contact, not a ninth signal pin. Coax shells used as the signal return are not separate shields.
Names beginning `br8d-i-` are interfaces; `br8d-o-` names are connector or cable forms. The safety and electrical limits are in the [architecture](../br8d-architecture.md).

applications.name: Candidate variants
notes: The entries are starting points, not a full list. A suffix such as `-2u-ABCV` gives the size and occupied pairs, not a complete pin map. Unless noted, a variant follows its family's map.

The boards target a 1U x 1U PCB (20.38 x 23.58 mm), connector at the north edge. Large connectors such as XLR and Speakon may need a bigger board or a panel mount. Check the part, header, clearances and enclosure before designing.

applications.name: Design inheritance
notes: Inheritance is a **design relationship**: a child is a different application name for a shared design, or a later specialization. A shared breakout must have the same connector, pin map and populated circuitry. A label or box can change the application name without changing the board.

**AUX TS -> CV TS:** `br8d-i-cv` TS boards share the `br8d-i-aux` TS design at levels 0-2, and CV specialization starts at level 3. For example, `br8d-i-cv-1ts-br0-1u-A` uses the same board as `br8d-i-aux-1ts-br0-1u-A`.
**AUX TRS -> CV TRS:** the four-TRS CV board has the same map as the balanced AUX board, so it can share it. The two-TRRS CV layout needs its own parent.
**Other overlaps:** mono RCA -> S/PDIF RCA; AUX TS -> S/PDIF TS; balanced XLR -> AES XLR. S/PDIF and AES need the right impedance and bandwidth, so check the part before reusing a board.
**Pin 2/3 swap:** audio XLR and DMX XLR swap pins 2 and 3 on A, so their boards are not interchangeable.
Share a file only when the physical design matches, including the shield path.
